2838.content: Verify webhook authenticity using HMAC-SHA256 signatures

2862.content: All webhook requests from Seal include an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the X-Seal-Signature header. Always verify this signature to ensure the request is authentic and hasn't been tampered with.

2863.content: Without signature verification, anyone who knows your webhook URL could send fake events to your endpoint. Signature verification ensures:

2864.content: Authenticity: The request came from Seal

2865.content: Integrity: The payload hasn't been modified

2868.content:
Security Critical: Never process webhook events without verifying the signature. Unverified
webhooks are a security vulnerability.

2869.content: Seal constructs a signed content string: {eventId}.{timestamp}.{payload}

2870.content: Seal generates an HMAC-SHA256 hash of that string using your webhook secret

2871.content: The signature is sent as v1={hex} in the X-Seal-Signature header, along with X-Seal-Event-Id and X-Seal-Timestamp headers

2872.content: Your server reconstructs the same signed content and generates the hash

2873.content: If the signatures match, the request is authentic
